title: Crane Brinton's last lecture on humanity's next evolutionary step
summary: Dan Sheehan tells of Crane Brinton's last lecture on humanity's next evolutionary step, about 1960s at Harvard, Cambridge, Massachusetts, and says they saw it or took part. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: and I had heard that crane Brinton uh who was the uh the chairman of the Department of intellectual history at Harvard
all this is 1968 right this is like May of 1968 and he says and I think that's why so many of you young men here refuse to go fight in this war in Vietnam ah wow that's said to us in that lecture
tellings.difference: Dates the lecture to May 1968 and adds the remark about refusing to fight in Vietnam.
tellings.link_reason: Sheehan goes on describing the same May 1968 lecture from telling 6, on an evolving human faculty and young men refusing the Vietnam war.

as_told.title: May 1968 lecture on an evolving faculty and Vietnam war refusal
as_told.place_text: lecture attended by the guest (US university)

plain: A man named Dan Sheehan told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that he was in the room at Harvard University for the last lecture of Crane Brinton, who he says was chairman of Harvard's department of intellectual history. Sheehan says Brinton spoke about humanity's next step in evolution. He dates it to May 1968 and says Brinton told the audience that this was why so many of the young men there refused to go and fight in the Vietnam War.
